/-
  Green's Theorem, rectangle case, Mathlib-native formalization.
  Freek Wiedijk's "100 theorems" entry #21.

  No custom axioms: integrals are `intervalIntegral`, partial derivatives
  are `deriv` applied to curried sections, smoothness is `ContDiff ℝ 1`
  on the uncurried map. The `rectLineIntegral` definition lives in
  `prereq.lean`.
-/

import prereq

open MeasureTheory intervalIntegral
open scoped Classical

/-- **Green's Theorem on a rectangle.** For continuously differentiable
    scalar fields `P, Q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ` and any rectangle $[a, b] \times [c, d]$,
    the counter-clockwise boundary line integral equals the
    $\partial_x Q$ double integral minus the $\partial_y P$ double
    integral:
    $$
    \oint_{\partial R} P\, dx + Q\, dy
      = \int_c^d \!\!\int_a^b \partial_x Q \,dx\,dy
        - \int_a^b \!\!\int_c^d \partial_y P \,dy\,dx.
    $$
    The two double integrals are stated in *different* orders of
    integration — each in the natural order for applying the FTC to
    its own partial derivative. By Fubini's theorem the two orders
    are interchangeable (under the smoothness hypothesis), so this
    statement is equivalent to the standard
    $\iint_R (\partial_x Q - \partial_y P)\,dA$. A follow-up lemma
    could derive that unified form from this one together with
    `intervalIntegral`-compatible Fubini. -/
theorem greens_theorem_rectangle_mathlib
    (P Q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (hP : ContDiff ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry P))
    (hQ : ContDiff ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry Q))
    (a b c d : ℝ) :
    rectLineIntegral P Q a b c d
      = (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x)
        - (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in c..d, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) := by
  -- Section smoothness: each curried section of P, Q is C¹.
  have hQxSec : ∀ y : ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x' => Q x' y) := by
    intro y
    have hpair : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x' : ℝ => (x', y)) :=
      ContDiff.prodMk contDiff_id contDiff_const
    have := hQ.comp hpair
    simpa [Function.uncurry] using this
  have hPySec : ∀ x : ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y' => P x y') := by
    intro x
    have hpair : ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun y' : ℝ => (x, y')) :=
      ContDiff.prodMk contDiff_const contDiff_id
    have := hP.comp hpair
    simpa [Function.uncurry] using this
  -- Inner FTC in x:  ∫ x in a..b, ∂ₓQ(x,y) = Q(b,y) − Q(a,y).
  have hQ_FTC : ∀ y : ℝ,
      (∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x) = Q b y - Q a y := by
    intro y
    apply integral_deriv_eq_sub
    · intro x _
      exact ((hQxSec y).differentiable
        (by norm_num : (1 : WithTop ℕ∞) ≠ 0)).differentiableAt
    · exact ((hQxSec y).continuous_deriv_one).intervalIntegrable a b
  -- Inner FTC in y:  ∫ y in c..d, ∂ᵧP(x,y) = P(x,d) − P(x,c).
  have hP_FTC : ∀ x : ℝ,
      (∫ y in c..d, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) = P x d - P x c := by
    intro x
    apply integral_deriv_eq_sub
    · intro y _
      exact ((hPySec x).differentiable
        (by norm_num : (1 : WithTop ℕ∞) ≠ 0)).differentiableAt
    · exact ((hPySec x).continuous_deriv_one).intervalIntegrable c d
  -- Rewrite the ∂ₓQ double integral using the x-FTC.
  have hQ_double :
      (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x)
        = (∫ y in c..d, Q b y) - (∫ y in c..d, Q a y) := by
    have eQ : (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x)
              = ∫ y in c..d, (Q b y - Q a y) := by
      simp_rw [hQ_FTC]
    rw [eQ]
    apply intervalIntegral.integral_sub
    · exact (hQ.continuous.comp
        (Continuous.prodMk (continuous_const : Continuous (fun _ : ℝ => b))
          continuous_id)).intervalIntegrable c d
    · exact (hQ.continuous.comp
        (Continuous.prodMk (continuous_const : Continuous (fun _ : ℝ => a))
          continuous_id)).intervalIntegrable c d
  -- Rewrite the ∂ᵧP double integral using the y-FTC.
  have hP_double :
      (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in c..d, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y)
        = (∫ x in a..b, P x d) - (∫ x in a..b, P x c) := by
    have eP : (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in c..d, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y)
              = ∫ x in a..b, (P x d - P x c) := by
      simp_rw [hP_FTC]
    rw [eP]
    apply intervalIntegral.integral_sub
    · exact (hP.continuous.comp
        (Continuous.prodMk continuous_id
          (continuous_const : Continuous (fun _ : ℝ => d)))).intervalIntegrable a b
    · exact (hP.continuous.comp
        (Continuous.prodMk continuous_id
          (continuous_const : Continuous (fun _ : ℝ => c)))).intervalIntegrable a b
  -- Unfold rectLineIntegral and close algebraically.
  unfold rectLineIntegral
  rw [hQ_double, hP_double]
  ring

/-- **Green's Theorem on a rectangle — unified form.** For continuously
    differentiable scalar fields `P, Q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ` whose partial
    derivatives are jointly continuous on the plane, and for any
    rectangle `[a, b] × [c, d]`, the counter-clockwise boundary line
    integral equals the standard double integral of `∂ₓQ - ∂ᵧP`:
    $$
    \oint_{\partial R} P\, dx + Q\, dy
      = \int_c^d \!\!\int_a^b \left(\partial_x Q - \partial_y P\right) dx\, dy.
    $$
    Derived from `greens_theorem_rectangle_mathlib` (the split form) via
    `intervalIntegral_swap_continuous` (Fubini for two interval integrals)
    and integral linearity.

    The joint continuity of `∂ₓQ` and `∂ᵧP` is stated as an explicit
    hypothesis; in a future refinement it could be derived from
    `ContDiff ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry P)` and `ContDiff ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry Q)`
    via the identification `deriv (section) = fderiv · (basis vector)`
    plus `ContDiff.continuous_fderiv`. -/
theorem greens_theorem_rectangle_unified
    (P Q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ)
    (hP : ContDiff ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry P))
    (hQ : ContDiff ℝ 1 (Function.uncurry Q))
    (hPy_cont : Continuous (Function.uncurry
        (fun x y => deriv (fun y' => P x y') y)))
    (hQx_cont : Continuous (Function.uncurry
        (fun x y => deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x)))
    (a b c d : ℝ) :
    rectLineIntegral P Q a b c d
      = ∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b,
          (deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x - deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) := by
  -- Start from the split form.
  rw [greens_theorem_rectangle_mathlib P Q hP hQ a b c d]
  -- Fubini swap on the ∂ᵧP term: (∫ x, ∫ y, ∂ᵧP) = (∫ y, ∫ x, ∂ᵧP).
  rw [show (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in c..d, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y)
        = (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) from
      (intervalIntegral_swap_continuous hPy_cont a b c d).symm]
  -- Integrability of the inner pieces (for each fixed y).
  have hQx_int : ∀ y : ℝ,
      IntervalIntegrable (fun x => deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x) volume a b := by
    intro y
    have : Continuous (fun x : ℝ => deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x) := by
      have := hQx_cont.comp (continuous_id.prodMk (continuous_const : Continuous (fun _ : ℝ => y)))
      simpa [Function.uncurry] using this
    exact this.intervalIntegrable a b
  have hPy_int : ∀ y : ℝ,
      IntervalIntegrable (fun x => deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) volume a b := by
    intro y
    have : Continuous (fun x : ℝ => deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) := by
      have := hPy_cont.comp (continuous_id.prodMk (continuous_const : Continuous (fun _ : ℝ => y)))
      simpa [Function.uncurry] using this
    exact this.intervalIntegrable a b
  -- Integrability of the parameter integrals on the outer interval.
  have hQx_outer :
      IntervalIntegrable
        (fun y => ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x) volume c d := by
    have hcont : Continuous
        (fun y : ℝ => ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x) := by
      have h : Continuous
          (Function.uncurry (fun y x : ℝ => deriv (fun x' => Q x' y) x)) := by
        have := hQx_cont.comp continuous_swap
        simpa [Function.uncurry] using this
      exact continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous' h a b
    exact hcont.intervalIntegrable c d
  have hPy_outer :
      IntervalIntegrable
        (fun y => ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) volume c d := by
    have hcont : Continuous
        (fun y : ℝ => ∫ x in a..b, deriv (fun y' => P x y') y) := by
      have h : Continuous
          (Function.uncurry (fun y x : ℝ => deriv (fun y' => P x y') y)) := by
        have := hPy_cont.comp continuous_swap
        simpa [Function.uncurry] using this
      exact continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous' h a b
    exact hcont.intervalIntegrable c d
  -- Merge the outer integrals via integral_sub (applied backwards).
  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_sub hQx_outer hPy_outer]
  -- Push the subtraction inside via integral_congr + inner integral_sub.
  refine intervalIntegral.integral_congr ?_
  intro y _
  simp only
  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_sub (hQx_int y) (hPy_int y)]

/-
  Prerequisites for theorem005 (greens_theorem_rectangle_mathlib).

  No custom axioms. Everything in `main.lean` is stated against Mathlib
  primitives:
    * `intervalIntegral` for 1D integrals
    * `deriv` applied to sections for partial derivatives
    * `ContDiff ℝ 1` for smoothness

  The only thing this file adds is a `def` for the counter-clockwise
  line integral around a rectangle, so that the main theorem can unfold
  it and expose the four summands.
-/

import Mathlib

open scoped Classical
open MeasureTheory intervalIntegral

/-- The line integral $\oint_{\partial R} (P\, dx + Q\, dy)$ around the
    boundary of the rectangle $R = [a, b] \times [c, d]$, traversed
    counter-clockwise starting from the bottom-left corner:

      bottom $(a, c) \to (b, c)$:  $\int_a^b P(x, c)\, dx$
      right  $(b, c) \to (b, d)$:  $\int_c^d Q(b, y)\, dy$
      top    $(b, d) \to (a, d)$:  $-\int_a^b P(x, d)\, dx$
      left   $(a, d) \to (a, c)$:  $-\int_c^d Q(a, y)\, dy$.

    The top and left segments pick up a minus sign because their
    orientations run "backwards" through the one-dimensional integrals,
    which are parameterized left-to-right / bottom-to-top. -/
noncomputable def rectLineIntegral
    (P Q : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ) (a b c d : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∫ x in a..b, P x c)
    + (∫ y in c..d, Q b y)
    - (∫ x in a..b, P x d)
    - (∫ y in c..d, Q a y)

/-- **Fubini for two `intervalIntegral`s under joint continuity.**
    For a jointly continuous real-valued function of two real arguments,
    the two orders of iterated `intervalIntegral` agree on any (possibly
    reversed) rectangle. This is the swap identity used to upgrade the
    split-form Green's theorem to its unified single-double-integral form. -/
lemma intervalIntegral_swap_continuous
    {f : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ} (hf : Continuous (Function.uncurry f)) (a b c d : ℝ) :
    (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b, f x y)
      = (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in c..d, f x y) := by
  have hmain :
      ∀ ⦃a b c d : ℝ⦄, a ≤ b → c ≤ d →
        (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b, f x y)
          = (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in c..d, f x y) := by
    intro a b c d hab hcd
    have hfi : IntegrableOn (Function.uncurry f) (Set.Icc a b ×ˢ Set.Icc c d) := by
      exact hf.continuousOn.integrableOn_compact (isCompact_Icc.prod isCompact_Icc)
    calc
      (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in a..b, f x y)
          = ∫ y in Set.Icc c d, ∫ x in Set.Icc a b, f x y := by
              simp only [intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hab, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hcd,
                setIntegral_congr_set (Ioc_ae_eq_Icc (α := ℝ) (μ := volume))]
      _ = ∫ z : ℝ × ℝ in Set.Icc c d ×ˢ Set.Icc a b, f z.2 z.1 := by
            exact (setIntegral_prod (fun z : ℝ × ℝ => f z.2 z.1)
              ((hf.comp continuous_swap).continuousOn.integrableOn_compact
                (isCompact_Icc.prod isCompact_Icc))).symm
      _ = ∫ z : ℝ × ℝ in Set.Icc a b ×ˢ Set.Icc c d, f z.1 z.2 := by
            simpa using
              (setIntegral_prod_swap (s := Set.Icc a b) (t := Set.Icc c d)
                (f := Function.uncurry f))
      _ = ∫ x in Set.Icc a b, ∫ y in Set.Icc c d, f x y := by
            exact setIntegral_prod (Function.uncurry f) hfi
      _ = (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in c..d, f x y) := by
            simp only [intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hab, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le hcd,
              setIntegral_congr_set (Ioc_ae_eq_Icc (α := ℝ) (μ := volume))]
  rcases le_total a b with hab | hab
  · rcases le_total c d with hcd | hcd
    · exact hmain hab hcd
    · apply neg_injective
      simpa only [intervalIntegral.integral_symm c d, intervalIntegral.integral_neg] using
        (hmain hab hcd : (∫ y in d..c, ∫ x in a..b, f x y) =
          (∫ x in a..b, ∫ y in d..c, f x y))
  · rcases le_total c d with hcd | hcd
    · apply neg_injective
      simpa only [intervalIntegral.integral_symm a b, intervalIntegral.integral_neg] using
        (hmain hab hcd : (∫ y in c..d, ∫ x in b..a, f x y) =
          (∫ x in b..a, ∫ y in c..d, f x y))
    · simpa only [intervalIntegral.integral_symm a b, intervalIntegral.integral_symm c d,
        intervalIntegral.integral_neg, neg_neg] using
        (hmain hab hcd : (∫ y in d..c, ∫ x in b..a, f x y) =
          (∫ x in b..a, ∫ y in d..c, f x y))
